user.text:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

history.assistant:
The book tracker is built, and I ran the whole flow against the production server: adding a book, marking it finished, opening its page, a bad link and a restart all worked. Start it with `npm run dev`, or `npm run build` then `npm start`, and open http://localhost:3000.

**What you get:**
- **Home page:** "Currently reading" and "Finished" lists, each with a "Mark as finished" button, and an "Add a book" form below. Title and author are required and notes are optional. If you leave a required field blank, you get an error message and the form keeps what you typed.
- **Book page (`/books/<id>`):** shows the title, author, when you started or finished, and your notes. It has a "Mark as finished" button and a "Copy link to share" button. Each book gets a random 8-character ID, so the links can't be guessed. A bad link shows a "Book not found" page.
- **Saving:** books are stored in `data/books.json`, which is created the first time you add one. Saves can't leave the file half-written, and two quick saves won't overwrite each other. If the file gets corrupted, the app shows an error rather than treating it as empty, so it won't wipe your books.

**Testing:**
- `npx vitest run`: 7 of 7 storage tests passed. Your `npm test` script runs the same thing.
- `npm run build`: passed with no warnings.
- Browser-free run-through against `next start`: I submitted the forms the way a browser does without JavaScript, then restarted the server and the book was still there. I haven't tried it in a real browser, so the copy-link button hasn't been clicked yet.

**Things to know:**
- **Sharing needs the app online.** A link to `localhost` only works on your own computer. And since there are no accounts, anyone who can reach the app can see every book, add books, and mark them finished, including whoever you send a link to.
- **Hosting:** the JSON file needs a server with its own permanent disk, like a small VPS. Serverless hosts like Vercel don't keep files written while the app runs.
- **Git:** `data/` is in `.gitignore`, so your books aren't committed. Remove that line if you want them in git as a backup.
- **Not included:** editing notes, deleting books, or moving a book back to "reading", since you didn't ask for them.

**Setup:** I installed Next 16.3.7 and React 19.3. I pinned TypeScript to 5.9.3 because TypeScript 7 doesn't work with `next build` yet. `npm audit` flags a moderate issue in the vitest version that was already in the project. Fixing it means a major vitest upgrade, so I left it alone. Nothing is committed.
